_what: A PARK CLEARED BY RULING — an ADDED artifact, never a deletion.
The five-round-park guard fires from the verdict files in .claude/skills/frame-critic/
history/. The only other way to clear it is to delete those files, and a mechanism whose
reset is 'destroy the record' teaches exactly the wrong reflex: the lane that most wants the
guard gone is the lane holding the evidence against itself. So every verdict stays on disk,
permanently readable, and this marker records where a ruling drew the line and why.
It cannot clear a BROKEN JUDGE. A soft critic is not a lane problem, and no ruling about a
lane makes an unreadable verdict readable.
ruling: The mottle is routed to the floor lane (floor-side, post-#169, measured) - your caps are
clean at 9 colours, faces frozen; you're not blocked by your own work, you're blocked by
the floor's, so hold for the combined build rather than running wall rounds that can't pass
Park cleared by ruling - author and commit PARK-CLEARED.json at repo root: quote this
ruling, state the blocking rounds (r002-r004, r006) judged an un-passable deck (dominant
defect belongs to the floor lane), guard counts judged rounds after the marker, no verdict
files deleted (evidence stays; the clear is an added artifact).
why_the_deck_was_un_passable: These four judged FAILs were rendered on a deck whose dominant defect was not this lane's
to fix. Measured on the delivered frames, unique colours by surface region:
The wall's colour count fell 43% when the cap was hard-snapped to the ladder (cap asset 107
-> 9 colours, against the approved ashlar floor's 8). Over the same span the FLOOR's count
more than doubled, 2209 -> 4708, on an eight-colour asset palette - arriving with the merge
of #169, on the floor lane's surface.
The frame critic named that layer as the single defect making the image read as filtered:
'The whole frame carries a soft continuous-tone mottle over the pixel work (5763 unique
colours against 2's 3414 for the same scene). Drop that layer; it's the single thing making
the image read as filtered.' Confirmed by measurement, and attributed to the floor.
A wall round cannot pass over another surface's defect. The rounds were not a lane failing
to converge; they were a lane being judged on a frame it did not control.
not_cleared: Nothing is deleted. r002, r003, r004, r005 (VOID) and r006 remain in history/ with their
verdicts, flip lists and build ids intact, and the guard still reads them - it simply counts
judged rounds AFTER round 6 when deciding whether this lane is getting anywhere.
The findings from those rounds that belong to this lane were acted on and are in the tree:
the sine-tooling self-catch, the hard-edge recovery (wall cells 4.6% -> 13.2% against the
last approved build's 10.7%), the slab/fracture architecture, and the palette snap.
next: HOLD for the combined build. No further wall rounds until the floor lane's continuous-tone
layer lands, per the same ruling.
